questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, leave extra space in front of your vehicle. Do not brake suddenly. Slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid a collision with the tailgater.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Brake lightly.
Do not use the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes during a skid. Using the brakes will make the skid worse.

questions.question: When exiting the interstate, when should you slow down?

options.text: About halfway through the deceleration lane.
As you approach the deceleration lane.
Right when you enter the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Keep your speed steady until you enter the deceleration lane. Then slow down to the posted speed for the exit ramp.

questions.question: If dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, you should drive slowly and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly. This helps other drivers see you too.

questions.question: If you cannot find a gap in freeway traffic to merge into, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to make room.
Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: Slow down on the ramp while waiting for a safe gap. Do not stop at the end of the ramp because you will not have enough room to speed up to match traffic before entering.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for people crossing.
No passing zone.
Construction or work zone ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction or work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This orange warning sign tells you that construction work is coming. Watch for temporary traffic control devices in the work zone.

questions.question: If you are under 21, your license can be suspended if you drive with a blood alcohol level of:

options.text: 0.15 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: There is zero tolerance for alcohol if you are under 21. Any amount of alcohol in your system will result in serious penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Give the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to be a problem.
Give the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to be a problem.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any vehicle that is close enough to cause a collision.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you on a two-lane road, what should you do?

options.text: Slowly reduce your speed so the tailgater will pass you.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Brake to slow down, then speed back up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly reduce your speed so the tailgater will pass you.
questions.explanation: Change lanes if possible. If you cannot change lanes, slowly reduce your speed. This will encourage the tailgater to pass you.

questions.question: If your vehicle has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what should you do when stopping on snow or ice?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal hard.
Do not use the brakes and let the car slow down on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal hard.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly on snow or ice. The ABS will pump the brakes faster than you can.

questions.question: When you prepare to turn left from a two-way street, where should you position your car?

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the centerline.
On the left side of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: For a left turn from a two-way street, start in the lane closest to the centerline. Begin your turn just before your car reaches the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first available legal lane.

questions.question: If there are no reduced speed signs in a work zone, what should you do?

options.text: Follow the normal speed limit.
Drive 15 mph slower than the posted speed limit.
Drive 15 mph faster than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the normal speed limit.
questions.explanation: Most work zones have signs showing lower speed limits. If there are no reduced speed signs in the work zone, follow the normal posted speed limit.

questions.question: On an interstate, how can you best avoid traffic merging from on-ramps on your right?

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Keep your speed and position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to the left.
questions.explanation: Watch for upcoming on-ramps on an interstate. When you can, move to the left lane to make room for vehicles entering from on-ramps on your right.

questions.question: A large truck ahead is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. What may happen?

options.text: The truck may finish its turn in either of the two lanes.
The truck may need to swing wide to complete the right turn.
The truck must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck may need to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need extra space to turn right, so they often swing wide to complete the turn.

questions.question: When a bicyclist makes a left turn, what may they do?

options.text: Use the left lane.
Cut through all lanes.
Wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride on the road with traffic. Expect to see bicyclists using the left lane when they turn left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions coming up. This sign warns you that another road crosses ahead.

questions.question: Why should you not use high beam headlights in fog or mist?

options.text: The light bounces back into your eyes.
Oncoming drivers might not see you.
Drivers behind you may follow too close.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light bounces back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beam headlights bounce back and reflect into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield the right-of-way.
No passing zone.
Fewer lanes ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangle sign means you must yield the right-of-way.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.
Check for drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check for other drivers trying to pass or enter your lane. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Never pass or change lanes in an intersection.

questions.question: If another driver is passing you in a no passing zone, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep your speed and position.
Slow down to let the other driver safely return to the driving lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to let the other driver safely return to the driving lane.
questions.explanation: Passing areas are based on how far drivers can see ahead. Help the passing vehicle return to the driving lane safely so everyone can avoid hazards.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a flashing red light at an intersection?

options.text: Stop completely. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians. Then go when it is safe.
Slow down and go ahead carefully.
Stop and stay stopped until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a full stop. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: You are entering the interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane. What should you do?

options.text: Go right into the traffic lane and speed up to match other cars.
Use the shoulder to reach the speed of traffic.
Speed up only after you see an open space in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you see an open space in traffic.
questions.explanation: On a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, speed up only after you find a gap in traffic. You may need to wait on the ramp for an opening to appear.

questions.question: You are driving defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car right in front of you.
Keep scanning for possible dangers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep scanning for possible dangers ahead.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking ahead for hazards. Do not just stare at the road directly in front of your car. Scan ahead and watch for traffic around you.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: You cannot pass.
You can pass on the right when the road is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can cross it to pass. You may pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.question: You park uphill on a road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight
Right, toward the edge of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels away from the center of the road. This way, if your brakes fail, your car will roll toward the side, not into traffic.
